notes: Lead: R. Chen (Head of Developer Experience). Use-case: in-IDE code assistant that can run tests, lints, and capture build logs via function/tool-calls to an isolated sandbox. Key asks: 1) function-calling primitives to invoke test-runner and return structured artifacts (exit codes, junit xml, stdout/stderr), 2) strict per-run sandboxing with no external network egress, 3) streaming logs back to the IDE with token-level low latency, 4) model/version pinning and controlled rollouts for agent behavior, 5) audit logs + KMS-backed artifact storage and 1-year retention. POC success criteria: a) developer can trigger `run_tests` from the assistant and see real-time logs in IDE with <200ms token latency for streaming chunks, b) each test run provisions an ephemeral container within 3s and completes without any outbound network access, c) artifacts are written to customer-owned storage with server-side-encryption, and audit entries are available for every function call. Quote from call: "We need per-test isolation — if a dev hits npm install it mustn't reach internet." Implementation notes: prefer Dedicated GPUs for low-latency completions in hosted mode; critical teams will require on-prem sandbox runners for sensitive repos. Model preferences: open-code model family preferred; ability to pin to vetted internal model and specify fallback to smaller hosted model if capacity constrained. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to reserved capacity for predictable latencies, but expect Optimize recommendations for batch sizing and KV caching. Integration wishlist: GitHub PR status integration, CI webhook to automatically run agent-created test suites, mapping build logs back to PR line numbers, and lint-fix suggestions as automated review comments. Action items: send detailed POC runbook and network egress template (AE), attach SOC2/ISO certs (SE), set up SSO test org for SAML verification.
